title: Architecture diagrams, decision records, design reviews, and production-readiness reviews
objectives: Select Salesforce Architecture Center diagram types (capability, landscape, solution, interaction process flow) for the question being asked.
Write architecture decision records that capture context, options, decision, and consequences—not a wiki afterthought.
Run a design review that uses Well-Architected Trusted/Easy/Adaptable and Decision Guides, not taste.
Define production-readiness as evidence: tests, Scale Test where required, security, rollback, observability—not a calendar date.
diagnostic_question: A squad wants to go live Friday with a new event-driven warehouse integration, no landscape diagram, no decision record for CDC versus platform events, and no Full-sandbox scale evidence. Which artifacts and reviews do you require before production-readiness?
definition: Architecture diagrams are the Architecture Center's standard views of topology, capability, process, and solution structure. Decision records capture a significant choice with context and consequences. Design reviews test a proposal against Well-Architected and Decision Guides before build hardens. Production-readiness reviews ask whether evidence (tests, scale, security, rollback, monitoring) exists to operate in production. ([Reference Diagrams](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/reference-diagrams/overview); [Well-Architected overview](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview.html))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail 'we talked about it' architectures. Diagrams without a decision record hide why CDC was chosen. Design reviews without Well-Architected become opinion. A go-live without production-readiness evidence is a scheduled incident. These artifacts are how CoE governance (ARCH-011) becomes visible.
sixty_second_explanation: Treat a Salesforce program like a building permit set. Diagrams are the stamped drawings: site plan (landscape), floor plan (solution), sequence of trades (interaction process flow). A decision record is the approved variance: why we used platform events instead of request/reply. Design review is plan check against code. Production-readiness is the occupancy inspection: smoke tests, load drill, keys, and a rollback—not the date on the invitation.
deeper_explanation: Salesforce Reference Diagrams give a shared visual language: capability maps, data-model notation, interaction process flows (including async, platform events, queues), solution architecture, system landscape (including org hierarchies and CoE), and roadmaps. Use the type that answers the stakeholder's question; do not paste one busy picture for every meeting. ([Reference Diagrams](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/reference-diagrams/overview))

Well-Architected organizes healthy solutions as Trusted, Easy, and Adaptable, with patterns and anti-patterns. Decision Guides (for example Event-Driven Architecture) exist to choose tools. A design review should cite those artifacts: Trusted (security, reliability), Easy (automated, engaging, performant), Adaptable (composable, resilient). ([Well-Architected overview](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview.html); [Event-Driven Decision Guide](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/decision-guides/guide/event-driven.html))

Architecture decision records (ADRs) are the team's durable memory of a significant, costly-to-reverse choice: context, options, decision, consequences, status. Salesforce does not ship a mandatory ADR object; the practice is how you keep diagrams honest. Link the ADR to the diagram and the package (ARCH-010).

Production-readiness is Well-Architected operationalized: Scale Test in Full sandbox when scale is an NFR (ARCH-009/011), failure mitigation, monitoring (Scale Center, Event Monitoring if licensed), security review, rollback, and no risky first-time production configuration. A design review that passed last quarter does not replace a readiness review against current evidence.

mental_model.analogy: Building permit set and occupancy inspection: drawings are architecture diagrams, variance forms are decision records, plan check is design review, occupancy inspection is production-readiness.
useful_mapping: system landscape → site plan (orgs, systems, trust boundaries)
capability map → what the building is for
solution architecture → floor plan of Salesforce components
interaction process flow → sequence of trades (including events)
decision record → approved variance with options and consequences
design review → plan check against Well-Architected code
production-readiness → occupancy inspection with tests and rollback
go-live date → invitation, not the inspection certificate
where_it_breaks: Software can iterate after occupancy; a concrete building cannot. ADRs must be amended, not frozen forever.
Salesforce has no single Setup object named ADR—this is a team practice.
A pretty diagram that contradicts the org is worse than no diagram.
Readiness is edition- and license-sensitive (Scale Test, Event Monitoring).

teach_back_prompt: Show which diagram you would bring to a CFO versus a developer, what belongs in a decision record for CDC versus REST, and what evidence a production-readiness review would refuse to skip.

review_schedule.prompt: Name four Reference Diagram types and one question each answers.
Write an ADR skeleton: context, options, decision, consequences.
Map Trusted / Easy / Adaptable to a design-review agenda.
List production-readiness evidence for an event-driven integration.
Two-minute interview: diagrams, ADRs, design review, production-readiness.

mermaid.structure:
flowchart TD
  Q[Stakeholder question] --> Diag[Architecture diagram type]
  Diag --> ADR[Decision record]
  ADR --> DR[Design review vs Well-Architected]
  DR --> Build[Build in non-prod]
  Build --> PRR[Production-readiness review]
  PRR --> Prod[Production]
  PRR --> Block[Not ready: missing evidence]
mermaid.decision:
flowchart TD
  Need[Need to communicate?] --> Q1{What question?}
  Q1 -->|Who talks to whom| Land[System landscape diagram]
  Q1 -->|How a process runs| Flow[Interaction process flow]
  Q1 -->|What we buy/build| Sol[Solution architecture]
  Choice[Significant tool choice] --> ADR[Write a decision record]
  Review[Before hardening code] --> DR[Design review citing Well-Architected / Decision Guides]
  GoLive[Want production?] --> PRR{Evidence: tests scale security rollback monitor?}
  PRR -->|Yes| Ready[Production-readiness pass]
  PRR -->|No| Wait[Do not confuse the date with occupancy]

claims.claim: Salesforce Reference Diagrams provide standard views: capability maps, interaction process flows (including events and async), solution architecture, system landscapes (including org hierarchies), and roadmaps. Choose the view that matches the question.
Well-Architected (Trusted, Easy, Adaptable) plus Decision Guides are the official compass for design reviews. They supply patterns and anti-patterns, not a substitute for org-specific NFRs.
claims.validation: Well-Architected overview and an example Decision Guide.

claims.claim: Production-readiness includes validating scalability with Scale Test before production when that NFR applies, plus failure mitigation and monitoring. Risky configuration must not appear first in production.
claims.validation: Reliable Scale Test guidance plus ALM no-prod-experiments pattern.

claims.claim: A Center of Excellence commonly owns review standards and training. Low-risk changes should not all wait on the same heavy review path (risk-based governance from ARCH-011).
claims.validation: CoE diagram plus ALM risk-based paths.

claims.claim: Architecture decision records are a team practice for significant choices (context, options, decision, consequences). Salesforce does not provide a single mandatory ADR sObject; mark productized ADR features as Needs verification if claimed.
claims.validation: Decision Guides show the kind of choice ADRs must freeze; ADR format is practice, not a Help object.

changed_in_release: Reverify Reference Diagram catalog names and Well-Architected URLs for Summer '26.
unresolved_uncertainty: There is no single official Salesforce Help article that mandates a specific ADR file format; teams should adopt one and keep it consistent.
Scale Test and Event Monitoring availability for a readiness checklist is license-specific.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Pick the right architecture diagram, write a decision record for costly choices, design-review against Well-Architected, and only then production-readiness with tests, scale evidence, security, rollback, and monitoring. The Friday date is not the certificate.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I bring a landscape to executives and a process flow to developers. The ADR states why CDC beat REST. Design review cites Trusted/Easy/Adaptable and the Decision Guide, not taste. Readiness asks for Full-sandbox scale if we claimed peak load, no first-time prod clicks, and a rollback. CoE sets the bar; not every report color needs a full architecture board.

terminology.plain: Standard pictures of the system so people share one map.
terminology.precise: Architecture Center types: capability, landscape, solution, interaction process flow, roadmap. Match the question; do not use one spaghetti slide.
terminology.example: System landscape showing Salesforce, warehouse, and EventBridge.
terminology.non_example: A screenshot of Setup as the landscape.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: ERD: data model, not the same as a landscape.
terminology.boundary: Use official notation when presenting to architects; informal sketches are for working sessions.

terminology.plain: A short paper on a choice we might regret forgetting.
terminology.precise: Context, options considered, decision, consequences, status. Linked to diagrams. Practice, not a standard Salesforce object.
terminology.example: ADR-014: CDC for Account replica; custom PE for warehouse code; Publish After Commit.
terminology.non_example: A Slack thumbs-up with no options listed.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Change set description: deployment, not architecture rationale.
terminology.boundary: Not every field needs an ADR—significant and costly-to-reverse.

terminology.plain: A structured look before the design hardens.
terminology.precise: Compare the proposal to Well-Architected pillars and relevant Decision Guides. Risk-based: CoE on high-risk, squad on low-risk.
terminology.example: Review of warehouse EDA against the Event-Driven Decision Guide.
terminology.non_example: A meeting that only debates color of a dashboard.
terminology.boundary: Passing design review does not equal production-readiness.

terminology.plain: Are we allowed to operate this in production now?
terminology.precise: Evidence: tests, scale (Full sandbox/Scale Test when NFR applies), security, monitoring, rollback, no first-time prod config. Date is not evidence.
terminology.example: Go/no-go with Scale Center baseline and rollback notes for LAB_ShipmentReady__e.
terminology.non_example: The sprint ends Friday so it must be ready.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Design review: intent versus operational evidence.
terminology.boundary: License gaps (no Scale Test) must be named as residual risk.

terminology.plain: Who talks to whom at the enterprise level.
terminology.precise: Reference Diagrams: Salesforce products, external systems, integration points, org hierarchies.
terminology.example: US prod, EU prod, ERP, EventBridge.

terminology.plain: The sequence of steps and messages.
terminology.precise: Reference Diagrams cover async, platform events, queues, pub/sub. Use when order and failure modes matter.
terminology.example: Order commit → After Commit PE → warehouse → status callback.
terminology.non_example: A capability map of 'Order to Cash' boxes only.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: UML sequence: similar intent; prefer Salesforce diagram language in CoE packs.
terminology.boundary: Does not replace an ADR for tool choice.

terminology.precise: Official framework of patterns/anti-patterns. Design reviews should name the pillar and the anti-pattern avoided.
terminology.example: Adaptable: unlocked package, not a monoflow.
terminology.non_example: We used Lightning so we are Well-Architected.
terminology.boundary: Framework is guidance; Salesforce does not auto-certify your org.

terminology.plain: A go-live party is not a readiness certificate.
terminology.precise: Handbook teaching phrase: the date is an invitation; production-readiness is the inspection. Not an official Salesforce object name.
terminology.example: Friday invite cancelled because Scale Test was in Developer sandbox.
terminology.boundary: Use in teaching; in interviews prefer 'readiness evidence.'

mechanics.after: Landscape for execs, process flow for builders

mechanics.failure: Same heavy board for a report color

mechanics.after: Evidence checklist pass or explicit residual risk

when_to_use: When stakeholders disagree about topology: produce architecture diagrams of the right type (landscape versus process flow).
When a tool choice is costly to reverse: write decision records (CDC vs REST, org split, package type).
When a design is about to harden: run a design review against Well-Architected and Decision Guides.
When a date is approaching: run a production-readiness review on evidence, not on the invitation.
when_not_to_use: Do not require a full architecture-board design review for a low-risk report color; use risk-based paths.
Do not treat a pretty diagram as a decision record if options and consequences are missing.
Do not call a sprint-end date a production-readiness pass without tests, rollback, and (when claimed) scale evidence.
Do not skip diagrams and ADRs because 'we are agile'; agility still needs a map and a memory.
configuration_or_code_location: Architecture Center Reference Diagrams and Well-Architected.
Team ADR repo (docs/adr or similar)—practice, not Setup.
Scale Center / Scale Test / sandbox evidence attached to the readiness packet.

worked_example.scenario: Warehouse EDA (from ARCH-007) wants Friday go-live. No landscape, no ADR for CDC vs custom PE, scale test was two clicks in a Developer sandbox. CoE can block. Lab is documentary; no production deploy.

decisions.decision: Require a system landscape plus an interaction process flow before design review.
decisions.because: Different questions: who integrates versus message order.

decisions.decision: ADR: CDC for Account/Order replica; custom PE After Commit for warehouse code; not UI request/reply.
Production-readiness fails until Full-sandbox scale evidence or an explicit residual-risk sign-off.
decisions.because: Reliable Scale Test; Developer sandbox is not scale testing.
decisions.rejected: Ship Friday because the sprint ends

configuration_or_code: Draft landscape and process-flow diagrams using Architecture Center types.
Write ADR-014 with options REST vs CDC vs PE.
Design-review agenda: Trusted (payload PII), Easy/Reliable (limits), Adaptable (package).
Readiness checklist: Apex tests, rollback, monitoring, Full sandbox plan.
worked_example.output: Go-live delayed or risk accepted in writing; artifacts exist.
verification: Readiness log states Developer sandbox is insufficient for the scale NFR.
worked_example.self_explanation: I separated design review (intent) from production-readiness (evidence) and forced an ADR for the event choice.

hands_on_lab.environment: Whiteboard or repo docs; no production org required.
starting_state_checks: You will not deploy to production.
steps: Pick a LAB_ initiative and name two diagram types you need and why.
Write a one-page decision record with at least two options.
Draft a five-bullet design-review agenda mapped to Trusted, Easy, or Adaptable.
Draft a production-readiness checklist including rollback and where scale evidence would come from.
guided_completion: If you only have a Developer sandbox, the checklist must say scale evidence is incomplete.
If CoE does not exist, say who plays that role.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Rewrite a fake ADR that only says 'we chose platform events' until it includes consequences.
evidence: Readiness checklist with a fail criterion.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Do not store real customer architecture in public repos.
hands_on_lab.limitations: Paper architecture; does not prove Scale Test access.

decision_table.signal: Executives ask which systems and orgs are in play.
decision_table.choose: System landscape architecture diagrams (and org hierarchy if multi-org).
decision_table.not: A Flow canvas or Setup screenshot.
decision_table.why: Reference Diagrams: landscapes answer topology questions.

decision_table.signal: Builders ask what happens when the order commits and the warehouse is down.
decision_table.choose: Interaction process flow plus a decision record on retry/idempotency.
decision_table.why: Process flows cover async/events; ADRs freeze the failure design.

decision_table.signal: CDC versus custom platform event versus REST spinner is still argued.
decision_table.choose: Decision record citing the Event-Driven Decision Guide; then design review.
decision_table.not: A diagram with no options or consequences.
decision_table.why: Diagrams show structure; ADRs show why.

decision_table.signal: Peak load was claimed but only a Developer sandbox was exercised.
decision_table.choose: Fail production-readiness (or written residual risk) until Full-sandbox/Scale Test evidence exists.
decision_table.not: Pass because the sprint ends Friday.
decision_table.why: Reliable and Resilient: scale testing is Full sandbox; date is not occupancy.

decision_table.signal: A report formula change with no integration or security NFR.
decision_table.choose: Lightweight path; skip a full architecture-board design review.
decision_table.not: The same board as a multi-org split.
decision_table.why: ALM risk-based paths; CoE should not bottleneck trivia.

limitations: ADR format is a practice, not a Salesforce object.
Does not replace legal or security sign-off templates.
security_notes: Landscapes should mark trust boundaries and data classes.
ADRs may mention PII in event payloads—restrict repo access.
Readiness includes least privilege, not only performance.
common_mistakes: One spaghetti diagram for every audience.
Same heavy review for every change.

troubleshooting.symptom: Two teams implemented different event tools for the same job.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The event bus picked for them.

troubleshooting.symptom: Go-live incident after a 'green' design review.
check: Readiness was not a separate gate.

troubleshooting.symptom: Reviews take six weeks for every field.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: More diagrams will speed it up.

production_notes: Attach diagrams and ADRs to the release record.
Re-run readiness if the design changed after the last review.
This lesson authorizes no production go-live.

mcqs.prompt: Which Architecture Center resource lists capability maps, landscapes, and process flows?
mcqs.rationale: Reference Diagrams overview is the catalog of those views.

mcqs.prompt: Well-Architected top-level pillars used in a design review?
mcqs.rationale: Well-Architected overview is organized around Trusted, Easy, Adaptable.

mcqs.prompt: A landscape diagram versus an interaction process flow?

options.A: Landscape: who/what systems; process flow: sequence including async/events
options.D: Landscape is only for Flow Builder

mcqs.rationale: Reference Diagrams separate system landscape from interaction process flows.

mcqs.prompt: Minimum contents of a useful architecture decision record?
mcqs.rationale: ADRs must preserve why, not only what. Salesforce does not ship a mandatory object; the practice still needs those fields.

distractor_explanations.C: A date is not a decision.

mcqs.prompt: Peak load claimed; only Developer sandbox was tested. Production-readiness?

options.A: Not ready (or residual risk must be explicit); scale testing belongs on Full sandbox
options.C: Ready if a landscape diagram exists

mcqs.rationale: Reliable/Resilient: Scale Test in Full sandbox. Date and diagrams are not scale evidence.

distractor_explanations.C: Diagrams are necessary but not sufficient.

mcqs.prompt: A design review for an event-driven warehouse should cite which kind of Architecture Center doc?

options.A: The Event-Driven Architecture Decision Guide (and Well-Architected)

mcqs.rationale: Decision Guides exist to choose EDA tools; Well-Architected is the review compass.

mcqs.prompt: Risky configuration first performed in production. Readiness view?

options.A: Fails ALM guidance; do not treat it as production-ready practice

mcqs.rationale: ALM anti-pattern: risky config in production.

mcqs.prompt: Report color change with no NFR. Full architecture-board design review?

options.C: Only if there is no CoE

mcqs.rationale: ALM: not every change uses the same path; CoE should not bottleneck trivia.

mcqs.prompt: Who often owns review standards and training?
mcqs.rationale: CoE diagram: standards, training, hard problems.

distractor_explanations.D: An environment, not a governance body.

mcqs.prompt: Design review passed last quarter; payload and volume changed. Production-readiness?

options.A: Re-run readiness against current evidence; old design review is not occupancy

mcqs.rationale: Readiness is current operational evidence; design review is earlier intent.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement separates review artifacts (metadata) from business data?

options.A: Diagrams and ADR files are documentation metadata in the repo; LAB_Order__c rows are business data

mcqs.rationale: Artifacts are documents/metadata; records are data.

mcqs.prompt: Scale Test before production supports which readiness concern?

options.A: Reliability/scalability evidence when that NFR applies

mcqs.rationale: Reliable: Scale Test in a test environment before production deploy.

interview_questions.question: Which architecture diagrams do you bring to which audience?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Landscape for executives (systems and orgs). Process flow for builders (sequence, events). Solution diagram for what we build on Salesforce. Not one spaghetti slide.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use Reference Diagrams types. Capability maps for scope. I refuse Setup screenshots as landscapes. I link diagrams to ADRs so the picture does not drift from the decision.
interview_questions.example: CFO sees US/EU boxes; developers see After Commit publish then warehouse.
follow_ups: What is a roadmap diagram for?

interview_questions.question: What belongs in an architecture decision record?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Context, options, the decision, and consequences. Status. Link to diagrams. Not a Slack thumbs-up.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I write ADRs for costly-to-reverse choices: org split, CDC vs PE, unlocked vs org-dependent. I cite Decision Guides. I admit Salesforce has no ADR sObject. I do not ADR a report color.
interview_questions.example: ADR-014 records CDC versus custom platform event versus a REST spinner for warehouse ship.
tradeoffs: Too many ADRs versus tribal knowledge
weak_answer_warnings: We do not write things down because we are agile

interview_questions.question: Warehouse EDA wants Friday go-live with no ADR and a Developer sandbox test. What reviews?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Design review against the EDA Decision Guide and Well-Architected. Production-readiness fails without Full-sandbox scale evidence if peak load was claimed.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I require landscape plus process flow, an ADR, and a readiness packet: tests, rollback, monitoring, security. I will not confuse the sprint date with occupancy. CoE can waive scale only as written residual risk, not as silence.
follow_ups: What if there is no Full sandbox SKU?
weak_answer_warnings: Ship because leadership already announced Friday

interview_questions.question: How do you run a design review that is not a taste contest?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Agenda mapped to Trusted, Easy, Adaptable, plus the relevant Decision Guide. Actions and owners. Risk-based attendance.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I ask which anti-patterns we are avoiding: monoflow, Publish Immediately on a query subscriber, Developer sandbox scale test. I keep low-risk changes off this board. I record the ADR number in the minutes.
interview_questions.example: Warehouse design review citing EDA guide After Commit.
weak_answer_warnings: I just know good architecture when I see it

interview_questions.question: Two integrations went live with different patterns for the same event. Root cause?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Missing decision record and skipped design review. Diagrams were not shared or did not show the channel.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I freeze an ADR now, even after the fact, and schedule a readiness look at duplicate side effects (idempotency). I do not add a third pattern. CoE updates standards so the next squad finds the record.
interview_questions.example: CDC and a custom PE both cloning Order fields.
follow_ups: How do you find existing events?
weak_answer_warnings: The platform should have stopped them

interview_questions.question: Incident after a green design review. What did you mix up?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Design review is intent. Production-readiness is evidence. Volume or security may have changed; first-time prod clicks may have happened.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I separate the gates. I re-run readiness. I check Scale Center. I look for ALM anti-patterns. I do not blame Well-Architected for skipping Scale Test.
interview_questions.example: Design approved in January; go-live in August with 10x volume.

interview_questions.question: When would you skip a heavy architecture design review?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Low-risk, reversible changes with no integration or security NFR—risk-based path. Still may need a tiny note, not a board.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I still want diagrams/ADRs for costly choices. I will not make report colors wait on the warehouse EDA board. CoE publishes the threshold. Skipping readiness for a peak-load feature is not the same as skipping a board for a formula.
weak_answer_warnings: Never review anything / review everything equally

interview_questions.question: Teach diagrams, ADRs, design review, and production-readiness with a building-permit analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Drawings, variance form, plan check, occupancy inspection. It breaks because software iterates after occupancy and Salesforce has no ADR object.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map landscape to site plan and process flow to trade sequence. I say Friday is an invitation. I cite Reference Diagrams and Well-Architected so it is not only a metaphor. I mention Full-sandbox scale as part of occupancy when we claimed peak load.
interview_questions.example: Warehouse EDA permit set versus Friday party.
